newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA FORAJ SUSPENDED FROM TRADING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA FORAJ SUSPENDED FROM TRADING.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Friday oil drilling company Foraj Sonde SA would be suspended from trading next week following a split of shares.

"Foraj will not be traded next Tuesday to give it time to register in the exchange's registry its new mass privatisation shareholders and the split of its listed shares," bourse general manager Stere Farmache told Reuters.

Foraj, a state-run company with a share capital of 16.5 billion lei, was part of a mass selloff which Romania launched in the autumn of 1995 offering around 15 million Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in around 4,000 state companies in exchange for coupons.
With the share-for-coupon offer oversubscribed, Foraj lowered its nominal share price to 1,000 lei from 25,000 to meet all bids.

To avoid coexistence on the bourse of shares of the same company at two different nominal values, 25,000 lei shares will be split, a bourse statement said, adding that one 25,000 lei share will be divided into 25 shares of 1,000 lei each.

The market price of Foraj split shares will be decided by the play of demand and offer when it rejoins trading, bourse spokesman George Chirita said, without giving a date for the resumption of trading in Foraj.
He said the new Foraj price would become the reference price for the following session.
At the bourse's latest session on Thursday Foraj closed at 6,360 lei, 550 lei stronger.
Brokers said the move would increase the company's liquidity but did not expect demand for its shares to increase substantially. They anticipated a new Foraj market price of around 200 lei.
